rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bird greets an Israelite king and asks leave to return to its fledglings until they grow, promising to return and submit to his judgment.
rows.anchor: السلام عليك أيها الملك المسلط على بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: فرقد السخي
rows.claim: Solomon says the bulbul's movements mean: it ate half a date, so the world may perish.
rows.anchor: وقال فرقد السخي: مر سليمان على بلبل فوق شجرة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: In Kaʿb's report, the warshan calls out that it wishes creatures had never been created.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن رجل عن كعب قال: صاحت ورشان عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: In Kaʿb's report, the peacock says that one who shows no mercy will receive no mercy.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن رجل عن كعب قال: صاحت ورشان عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: In Kaʿb's report, the sird tells sinners to seek forgiveness; the report says the Prophet therefore forbade killing it.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن رجل عن كعب قال: صاحت ورشان عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: In Kaʿb's report, the titwi says every living thing dies and every new thing wears out.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن رجل عن كعب قال: صاحت ورشان عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: In Kaʿb's report, the swallow urges people to send good deeds ahead to find them; the report says the Prophet forbade killing it.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن رجل عن كعب قال: صاحت ورشان عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: In Kaʿb's report, the pigeon says: Glory be to my Lord Most High, filling His heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن رجل عن كعب قال: صاحت ورشان عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qamari bird says, ‘Glory be to my Lord Most High.’
rows.anchor: وصاح قمري عند سليمان (عليه السلام)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crow calls down a curse upon tax collectors.
rows.anchor: والغراب يدعو على العشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kite says that everything perishes except God.
rows.anchor: والحدأة تقول: كل شيء هالك إلا الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sandgrouse says that whoever stays silent is safe.
rows.anchor: والقطاة تقول: من سكت سلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parrot warns that woe awaits the person whose concern is worldly life.
rows.anchor: والببغاء تقول: ويل لمن الدنيا همه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The frog says, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Holy.’
rows.anchor: والضفدع يقول: سبحان ربي القدوس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The falcon says, ‘Glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him.’
rows.anchor: والبازي يقول: سبحان ربي وبحمده،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The female frog glorifies the One remembered everywhere.
rows.anchor: والضفدعة تقول: سبحان المذكور بكل مكان.

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhul reports that the durraj calls out, ‘The All-Merciful is established over the Throne.’
rows.anchor: عن مكحول قال: صاح دراج عند سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when a rooster crows, it tells heedless people to remember God.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الديك إذا صاح يقول:

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reports that the eagle's call tells Adam's child to live as desired, since death is the end.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي قال: إذا صاح النسر قال: يا ابن آدم عش ما شئت آخره الموت

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reports that the ʿuqab says that distance from people brings companionship.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي قال: إذا صاح النسر قال: يا ابن آدم عش ما شئت آخره الموت

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reports that the bird called al-qabr asks God to curse those who hate the family of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي قال: إذا صاح النسر قال: يا ابن آدم عش ما شئت آخره الموت

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reports that the swallow recites the Opening of the Book, prolonging its final word as a reciter does.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي قال: إذا صاح النسر قال: يا ابن آدم عش ما شئت آخره الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon assembled his forces of jinn, humans, and birds; they were held back until the whole group gathered, with supervisors keeping each rank in order as royal armies do.
rows.anchor: وحشر وجمع لسليمان جنوده من الجن والإنس والطير في مسير لهم فهم يوزعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses yūzaʿūn as being pushed back.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: يوزعون: يدفعون.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Muqatil gloss yūzaʿūn as being driven along.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد ومقاتل: يساقون،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses yūzaʿūn as being stopped or held in place.
rows.anchor: السدي: يوقفون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of wazʿ in Arabic means restraint or prevention; awzaʿahu can also mean to incline or prompt someone toward a matter.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوزع في كلام العرب الكف والمنع، ومنه الحديث: ما يزع السلطان أكثر مما يزع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usage illustrates the root with the saying that a ruler restrains more than the Qur'an and the maxim that people need preventers.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر: لا بد للناس من وزعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse of poetry uses wāziʿ for a restraining or admonishing force against youthful impulse.
rows.anchor: على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا … وقلت

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb describes Solomon traveling with his household and officials on stacked canopies, accompanied by kitchens, ovens, huge cauldrons, animal grounds, and wind-borne transport between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه عن كعب قال:

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Passing Medina, Solomon identifies it as the migration home of a future prophet and blesses whoever believes in and follows him.
rows.anchor: فقال سليمان: هذه دار هجرة نبي في آخر الزمان، طوبى لمن آمن به،

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb's account says the Kaaba wept because Solomon and his righteous company passed without worshipping there while idols were worshipped nearby; God promises it worshippers, a final prophet, a new scripture, and purification from idols.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله سبحانه إلى البيت: ما يبكيك؟ فقال: يا رب أبكاني هذا نبي من أنبيائك

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb's story places the ant valley near Wadi al-Sadir at Taif and describes an enormous, limping ant warning its fellows to enter their homes lest Solomon's forces crush them unknowingly.
rows.anchor: ثم مضى سليمان حتى مر بوادي السدير، واد من الطائف فأتى على واد النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind carried every creature's speech to Solomon; understanding the ant, he smiled and prayed to be enabled to give thanks and join God's righteous servants, meaning the monotheists.
rows.anchor: يعني أن سليمان يفهم مقالتها وكان لا يتكلم خلق إلا حملت الريح ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatada and Muqatil locate the Valley of the Ants in Syria.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: وادي النمل بأرض الشام.

rows.speaker: نوف الحميري
rows.claim: Nawf al-Himyari says the ants in Solomon's valley were like flies.
rows.anchor: قال نوف الحميري: كان نمل وادي سليمان مثل الذباب

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the ant whose speech Solomon understood had wings.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: النملة التي فقه سليمان كلامها كانت ذات جناحين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Solomon heard the ant from three miles away.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: سمع سليمان كلامها من ثلاثة أميال

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the ant's name as Tahiyah.
rows.anchor: عن أبي روق عن الضحاك قال:

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil gives the ant's name as Harami.
rows.anchor: اسم نملة سليمان حرمي، وهو قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account in some books says the ant defended her warning: she feared not crushed bodies but hearts distracted from praising God by wishing for Solomon's gifts; she then admonished him about mortality and the fleeting world through wordplay on David, Solomon, and the wind.
rows.anchor: خشيت أن يتمنين ما أعطيت ويشتغلن بالنظر عن التسبيح، فقال لها: عظيني،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet forbade killing four creatures: the hoopoe, sird, bee, and ant.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل أربعة من الدواب: الهدهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Solomon was told the future prophet would appear in about a thousand years and that Muhammad would be the chief and seal of the messengers.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وكم بيننا وبين خروجه يا نبي الله؟ قال: زهاء ألف عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After performing the pilgrimage at Mecca, Solomon traveled to Yemen and reached Sana'a at noon in a day's journey, though the route usually took a month; the lush land pleased him, but he could find no water.
rows.anchor: فخرج من مكة صباحا وسار نحو اليمن يوم نجم سهيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe served as Solomon's water guide: it could see subterranean water as plainly as a cup in one's hand, mark its location and depth by pecking, and demons would dig it out.
rows.anchor: وكان الهدهد دليله على الماء، كان يرى الماء من تحت الأرض كما يرى أحدكم كأسه بيده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq challenges Ibn Abbas: if the hoopoe sees underground water, why does it fail to see grain and get caught? Ibn Abbas answers that destiny can obstruct sight.
rows.anchor: فقال له نافع بن الأزرق: فرأيت قولك الهدهد ينقر الأرض فيبصر الماء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports through Qatada that the Prophet forbade killing the hoopoe because it guided Solomon to nearby and distant water and wanted God to be worshipped on earth.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تقتلوا الهدهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story names Solomon's hoopoe Yaʿfur and the Yemeni hoopoe ʿAnfar; ʿAnfar says Bilqis rules the land, commands twelve thousand leaders each over one hundred thousand fighters, and controls the sun.
rows.anchor: وكان اسم هدهد سليمان بن داود عليه السلام: يعفور، واسم هدهد اليمن عنفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Yemeni hoopoe persuades Yaʿfur to visit Bilqis, saying Solomon will welcome news of her; Yaʿfur fears missing the water needed at prayer, but returns at afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: قال الهدهد اليماني: إن صاحبك ليسره أن تأتيه بخبر هذه الملكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When water is unavailable and the hoopoe is missing, Solomon questions the eagle, overseer of the birds; the eagle disclaims knowledge, and Solomon threatens severe punishment or slaughter unless the hoopoe brings clear proof.
rows.anchor: فسأل الإنس عن الماء فقالوا: ما نعلم هاهنا ماء. فسأل الجن والشياطين فلم يعلموا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports from Ibn Abbas that every occurrence of sultan in the Qur'an means proof or evidence.
rows.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: كل سلطان في القرآن فهو حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon sends the ʿuqab to retrieve the hoopoe; it surveys the world from the air, spots the returning bird from Yemen, and dives toward it.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا بالعقاب سيد الطير فقال: علي بالهدهد الساعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe pleads with the pursuing ʿuqab by God who empowered it; the ʿuqab relents but warns that Solomon has sworn to punish or kill it unless it gives a clear excuse.
rows.anchor: فناشده فقال: بحق الله الذي قواك فأقدرك علي إلا رحمتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe confirms that Solomon allowed the alternative of bringing a clear excuse; the ʿuqab brings it back to Solomon.
rows.anchor: فقال الهدهد: أوما استثنى رسول الله؟ قالوا: بلى، قال: أو ليأتيني بعذر بين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe approaches Solomon humbly, asks him to remember standing before God, and Solomon trembles at the reminder and pardons it.
rows.anchor: يا نبي الله اذكر وقوفك بين يدي الله سبحانه، فلما سمع ذلك سليمان ارتعد وعفا عنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says that after Bilqis's father died without a son, factional conflict split Yemen; she married the abusive ruler by a ruse, killed him while he was drunk, and the people then made her queen.
rows.anchor: قالوا: فلما مات أبو بلقيس ولم يخلف ولدا غيرها طمعت في الملك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Bakra reports that when Bilqis was mentioned, the Prophet said a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will not prosper.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكرة قال: ذكرت بلقيس عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqis had every kind of equipment and provision that kings need.
rows.anchor: وأوتيت من كل شيء يحتاج إليه الملوك من الآلة والعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madyan's water was a well, where people watered their livestock; the two women stood apart restraining their sheep from straying.
rows.anchor: ولما ورد ماء مدين وهو بئر كانت لهم وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون مواشيهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the women kept their sheep from mixing with other people's flocks; the mention of sheep is omitted for brevity.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: تكفان [أغنامهما] عن أن تختلط بأغنام الناس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the women were keeping the people away from their sheep.
rows.anchor: قتادة: [تذودان] الناس عن شائهما

rows.speaker: أبو مالك وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Malik and Ibn Ishaq say they kept their flock back until the shepherds had left the water, then watered it because they were weak; the author prefers this as it best fits what follows.
rows.anchor: أبو مالك وابن إسحاق: تحبسان غنمهما عن الماء حتى يصدر عنه مواشي الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khatb means their situation or business: why were they not watering their livestock with the others?
rows.anchor: ما خطبكما ما شأنكما لا تسقيان مواشيكما مع الناس

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وابن عامر وابن جعفر وأيوب بن المتوكل
rows.claim: These readers open the yāʾ and damma the dāl, making the shepherds the subject: the women wait until the shepherds return from the water.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وابن عامر وابن جعفر وأيوب بن المتوكل: بفتح الياء وضم الدال

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers damma the yāʾ and kasra the dāl, meaning the shepherds drive their livestock away from the water.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بضم الياء وكسر الدال أي حتى يصرفوا مواشيهم عن الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿi, on the pattern of tujjar from tājir; the women cannot compete with the men and water only after the shepherds leave the flock's remainder in the trough.
rows.anchor: والرعاء: جمع راع مثل تاجر وتجار، ومعنى الآية لا نسقي مواشينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father is too old to water his livestock himself.
rows.anchor: وأبونا شيخ كبير لا يقدر أن يسقي مواشيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي والحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Hasan identify their father as the prophet Shuʿayb, named Shuʿayb ibn Buwayb ibn Midyan ibn Abraham.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد والضحاك والسدي والحسن:

rows.speaker: وهب وسعيد بن جبير وأبو عبيدة بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Wahb, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Abu ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbd Allah identify the father as Buthrun, Shuʿayb's nephew; Shuʿayb had died blind and was buried between the Maqam and Zamzam.
rows.anchor: قال وهب وسعيد بن جبير وأبو عبيدة بن عبد الله: هو بثرون ابن أخي شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daughter cites Moses's strength: he removed a rock from the well that, she says, only forty men could lift.
rows.anchor: فهل بقربكما بئر؟ قلنا: نعم، ولكن عليها صخرة لا يرفعها إلا أربعون رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She cites Moses's trustworthiness: he told her to walk behind him and throw a pebble ahead if she needed to direct his path.
rows.anchor: وأما أمانته فإنه قال لي في الطريق: امشي خلفي، وإن أخطأت فارمي قدامي بحصاة

rows.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
rows.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi names Moses's wife Safura and her sister Labani.
rows.anchor: قول شعيب الجبائي قال: امرأة موسى صفورة،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the daughters Safura and Sharafa.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: صفورة وشرفا،

rows.speaker: غيرهم
rows.claim: Other authorities say the elder daughter was Safra and the younger Safira.
rows.anchor: وغيرهما: الكبرى صفرا والصغرى صفيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾjurni means ajirni, ‘hire me’; the verb can also be used of God rewarding someone.
rows.anchor: قال: [يقول العرب] آجرك الله فهو يأجرك بمعنى أثابك

rows.speaker: الأئمة
rows.claim: The authorities say that tending the father's livestock for eight years was the payment serving as the marriage dowry.
rows.anchor: قالت الأئمة: على أن تثيبني من تزويجها رعي ماشيتي ثماني حجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥijja here means a year, and ḥijaj is its plural.
rows.anchor: ثماني حجج سنين واحدتها حجة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra two years are a voluntary favor from Moses, not a condition stipulated in the marriage contract.
rows.anchor: وأنت به متبرع متفضل وليس مما اشترطه عليك في عقد النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father promises not to burden Moses and says he will be among the righteous by keeping his agreement and treating him well.
rows.anchor: ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين من الوافين بالعهد، المحسنين الصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agreement is between the two men; whichever term Moses fulfills, eight or ten years, brings no reproach, and God is witness and guardian of their words.
rows.anchor: أيما الأجلين قضيت الثمان أو العشر فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Adam brought Moses's staff from Paradise and Gabriel took it after Adam's death, keeping it until he met Moses at night and handed it to him.
rows.anchor: فقال عكرمة: خرج بها آدم من الجنة وأخذها جبريل بعد موت آدم

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say prophets inherited the staff until it reached Shuʿayb, who held the prophets' staffs and gave one to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: لم يزل الأنبياء يتوارثونها حتى وصلت إلى شعيب وكانت عصي الأنبياء عنده

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi tells how an angel entrusted the staff to Shuʿayb; his daughter repeatedly could take only that staff for Moses, and Shuʿayb later disputed its ownership with Moses and sought an arbitrator.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: كانت تلك العصا استودعها ملك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: In al-Suddi's staff story, an angel arbitrates that whichever man can lift the staff from the ground owns it; Shuʿayb cannot lift it, but Moses can.
rows.anchor: ضعوها بالأرض فمن حملها فهي له، فعالجها الشيخ فلم يطقها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's account says Yathrun had thirteen staffs in a private room; his eleven sons each burned and died after being sent to retrieve one, while Moses took a staff for herding, leading Yathrun to recognize him as a prophet.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: كان في دار يثرون بيت لا يدخله إلا يثرون وابنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another story says Shuʿayb sent Moses left at a fork to avoid a dragon, but the sheep went right; while Moses slept, his staff killed the dragon and returned bloody.
rows.anchor: فإن هناك تنينا عظيما أخشى عليك وعلى الأغنام منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses sees the dead dragon and bloody staff as a sign of God's power; Shuʿayb, who is blind, finds the sheep healthier, then offers Moses that year's piebald young goats as a reward for his herding.
rows.anchor: فعاد إلى شعيب، وكان شعيب ضريرا فمس الأغنام، فإذا هي أمثل حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to strike the water at the flock's watering place.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك الماء الذي في مستقى الأغنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses strikes the water, and every ewe bears a piebald offspring; Shuʿayb recognizes this as provision from God for Moses and his wife, fulfills his bargain, and hands over the flock.
rows.anchor: فضرب موسى بعصاه الماء ثم سقى الأغنام منه، فما أخطأت واحدة منها إلا وقد

rows.speaker: الحارث بن عثمان بن نوفل بن عبد مناف
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Harith ibn ʿUthman ibn Nawfal: he told the Prophet they knew his message was true but feared Arabs would seize Mecca if they followed him, since the tribes opposed them and they could not resist.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الحارث بن عثمان بن نوفل بن عبد مناف وذلك أنه قال للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had established Mecca as a secure sanctuary: while pre-Islamic Arabs raided and killed one another, people of Mecca remained safe wherever they went because of the sanctuary's inviolability.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن العرب في الجاهلية كان يغير بعضهم على بعض، فيقتل بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
rows.claim: The readers of Medina and Yaʿqub read tajbā with tāʾ to agree with the feminine thamarāt; Abu Hatim prefers this reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب (تجبى) بالتاء لأجل الثمرات واختاره أبو حاتم

rows.speaker: غيرهم
rows.claim: Other readers use the masculine verb yujbā; Abu ʿUbayd prefers it because an intervening phrase separates the verb from the feminine noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ غيرهم بالياء كقوله كل شيء واختاره أبو عبيد قال: لأنه قد حال بين الاسم المؤنث والفعل حائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Batarat means that a town's inhabitants rejoiced insolently and transgressed, disbelieving in their Lord.
rows.anchor: بطرت معيشتها، أي أشرت وطغت، فكفرت بربها

rows.speaker: عطاء بن رياح
rows.claim: ʿAta ibn Riyah explains that the people lived arrogantly and extravagantly, consumed God's provision, and worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء بن رياح: أي عاشوا في البطر والأشر وأكلوا رزق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine verb is grammatically assigned to the town, although the people are the actual subjects; the people are omitted for concision.
rows.anchor: وجعل الفعل للقرية وهو في الأصل للأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few of the ruined towns were inhabited afterward; most remained deserted.
rows.anchor: فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا يعني فلم يعمر منها إلا أقلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says only travelers and passersby stayed in those towns, for a day or an hour.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يسكنها إلا المسافر ومار الطريق يوما أو ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God inherits the towns is compared with the verses saying God inherits the earth and all it contains, and that the inheritance of the heavens and earth belongs to God.
rows.anchor: نظيره قوله سبحانه: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وقوله: ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not destroy towns for their people's disbelief before sending a messenger to their principal town—Mecca—to recite His signs; destruction falls only on wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى بكفر أهلها حتى يبعث في أمها يعني مكة رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever people receive is only the enjoyment and adornment of worldly life; what God has is better and more enduring, so people should reason.
rows.anchor: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads the verb with yāʾ: ‘Do they not reason?’
rows.anchor: أفلا تعقلون بالياء أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use tāʾ: ‘Will you not reason?’
rows.anchor: يختلف عنه الباقون بالتاء
